name: Bog
notes: Ombrotrophic raised/blanket bog: rain-fed acid peat, Sphagnum carpets, cottongrass, heath dwarf shrubs, carnivorous sundews, stunted bog pines. Drawn on Scandinavia/British Isles/Baltic and Canadian muskeg.

canopy.name: Black spruce
canopy.source: Picea mariana, dominant stunted tree of N American bog/muskeg 2-10 m, narrow spire

traits.native_range: Picea mariana, dominant stunted tree of N American bog/muskeg 2-10 m, narrow spire
traits.leaf_shape: needles or scale leaves, evergreen (larch deciduous)
traits.trunk: single straight trunk, whorled branches, conical crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: thin grey-brown bark in small flaky scales over olive-green inner bark

canopy.silhouette: narrow dark spire with a clubbed top

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny epigeal seedlings on moss grow only 2.5-15 cm a year. Saplings are narrow, spindly spires with short blue-green needles and a dense, club-like top; lower branches drooping onto the moss often root (layering), ringing an old tree with young clones. Mature trees look like bottle-brushes with a knob of cones at the top.
growth.source: USDA Silvics (Viereck & Johnston): seedlings 2.5 cm/yr on moss, to 15 cm on mineral soil; 12-20 m on good sites; main cone-bearing age 30-250; establishes in 10% of full light; layering common; average max age ~200, up to 280 years

fruiting.source: USDA Silvics (pollen late May-early June; cones 1-4 cm, green or purplish when young, seed mature late Aug-early Sep; semi-serotinous cones stay partly closed on the tree for years, holding viable seed up to 25 years and releasing it gradually or after fire; heavy crops every 2-6 years)

bark.note: lower trunk grey-brown and fissured into plates; upper trunk and branches flaking orange-red

canopy.silhouette: stunted twisted pine with an orange upper trunk

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with 5-7 cotyledons; in its first year it has single, flat, finely serrated primary needles 2-3 cm long, then short, twisted, blue-green paired needles. Young trees are regular, bushy cones; later the lower branches drop and the crown becomes flat or rounded above a tall trunk whose upper bark is orange and flaky.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 35 m, over 45 m on the best sites; normally lives 150-300 years, over 760 in Lapland; first-year seedlings have single serrated leaves 2-3 cm; seeds released 22-24 months after pollination); growth and first cones from European yield tables

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (pollen released mid to late spring; first-year conelets globose, 4-8 mm; mature cones 3-7.5 cm, green then grey-green to yellow-brown; seeds released 22-24 months after pollination); crop and decay estimated

traits.native_range: Larix laricina, Canada/NE USA bogs and fens, deciduous conifer 3-15 m turning gold

leaf.note: soft light blue-green needles in spur tufts of 15-30 (schema caps fascicle at 8), single on long shoots; deciduous, gold in autumn

bark.note: thin, grey on young trees, red-brown and flaking in small scales on mature trunks

canopy.silhouette: thin open spire, gold in autumn

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: about six needle-like cotyledons; in full light first-year seedlings reach only 18-23 cm with soft single needles, and 46-64 cm by year three. Young trees are narrow, open, feathery cones of tufted blue-green needles that turn bright gold and drop in autumn; under a canopy they die, so they must stay in the open.
growth.source: USDA Silvics of North America vol. 1 (Larix laricina: germination late May-mid June, epigeal; seedlings 18-23 cm yr 1, 46-64 cm yr 3; mature 15-23 m; viable seed at 12-15 yr, large crops from ~40; good crops every 3-6 yr; usually 150-180 yr, max 335; very intolerant of shade).

fruiting.source: USDA Silvics (flowers late Apr-early May; cones ripen Aug-Sep, brown, oblong-ovoid, 13-19 mm; seed shed Sep through spring; vigorous open-grown trees up to 20,000 cones a year). Young-cone colour, set and persistence estimated.

shrub.name: Bog myrtle
shrub.source: Myrica gale, N Europe and N America bog margins and wet heath, aromatic deciduous shrub 0.5-2 m

traits.native_range: Myrica gale, N Europe and N America bog margins and wet heath, aromatic deciduous shrub 0

leaf.note: oblanceolate, toothed only toward the apex, dotted with yellow resin glands, grey-green

bark.note: dark red-brown smooth stems with pale lenticels and resin glands

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling on wet peat or sandy lake shores; leaves narrowly wedge-shaped, toothed near the tip, grey-green and dotted with fragrant resin glands, as in the adult. It branches from the base into an upright, reddish-brown-twigged little bush and spreads by root suckers into dense clonal thickets; nitrogen-fixing root nodules help it on poor bog soils.
growth.source: Wikipedia Myrica gale (deciduous shrub to 2 m; catkins before the leaves, male yellowish to orange-brown, female red to purple; usually dioecious but plants may change sex from year to year; dense clonal colonies from root suckers); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Myrica (1-6 ft); ages estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (catkins in spring before the leaves, several per twig; red-purple female catkins; small waxy fruits). Here one 'flower' is a female catkin and one 'fruit' the small brown cone-like head it becomes, of 2-3 mm resin-dotted winged nutlets that float off in water; ripe late summer, persists into winter; set and crop estimated

shrub.name: Bog rosemary
shrub.source: Andromeda polifolia, circumboreal bogs, low evergreen shrub 10-40 cm with pink bell flowers

traits.native_range: Andromeda polifolia, circumboreal bogs, low evergreen shrub 10-40 cm with pink bell flowers
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: narrow leathery evergreen leaves with strongly revolute margins, blue-green above, white beneath

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: radicle first, two tiny cotyledons 11 days later, first true leaves at 18-28 days; at 6 weeks it is a slender upright shoot 1-2 cm tall on wet moss. It becomes sparse, upright woody stems with narrow, leathery, blue-green leaves with rolled-under edges and chalky-white undersides, creeping by rhizomes through sphagnum.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Andromeda polifolia: mean germination 13 d, light-dependent (66.5% at 25 C in light, 24-27% in shade or dark); cotyledons 11 d and first leaves 18-28 d after the radicle, a 1-2 cm shoot at 6 wk; plants 5-80 cm; shade intolerant. Growth rate, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Andromeda polifolia: 1-4 nodding urn-shaped flowers in terminal clusters, May-Aug by region; pollinated by bumblebees, honeybees, syrphid flies and butterflies; capsules 3-6 mm, 1-44 seeds, mature late Jul-Aug and often persist into winter. Fruit set and crop estimated; foliage contains grayanotoxins.

traits.native_range: Vaccinium oxycoccos, circumboreal Sphagnum bogs, creeping vine on moss carpets with red berries

leaf.note: tiny evergreen leaves with revolute margins, dark glossy green above, whitish beneath, on wiry trailing stems

growth.juvenile_note: A minute seedling on wet sphagnum: two tiny cotyledons, then a hair-thin wiry stem with small pointed leaves, dark green above and whitish beneath with rolled edges. It creeps over and through the moss instead of rising, rooting at the nodes, so a young plant is a loose web of thread-like reddish runners a hand-width across with a few short upright leafy tips.
growth.source: USDA FEIS (Vaccinium oxycoccos): seed needs cold after-ripening (6-7 months at 0 C) before germinating at 25 C, shade intolerant, spreads by rhizomes and runners, flowers and fruits profusely 1-3 years after fire. Height given as mat spread; seedling growth, first flowering and ages estimated from the genus and V. macrocarpon.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (Vaccinium oxycoccos): pink to red flowers borne singly or in clusters at stem ends, June-July; self-pollinating but insects, especially bees, raise seed set; red juicy berries ripen Aug-Oct and often persist through winter. Flower size (reflexed petals), fruit set, fruit size, rot time and crop estimated.

traits.native_range: Calluna vulgaris, dominant on British/Scandinavian blanket bog hummocks, evergreen 20-60 cm, purple flowers

leaf.note: tiny scale leaves in four ranks, closely pressed to the twig

bark.note: old woody stems dark grey-brown, rough, bark shredding in thin strips

growth.juvenile_note: Dust-fine seeds need light and sprout in 2-6 weeks on bare peat, sand or burnt ground. The seedling is a tiny green sprig of minute, overlapping, scale-like leaves in four rows; it branches into a small upright bush (pioneer phase), then a dense, rounded dome (building phase) that later spreads, thins and opens in the centre as it ages.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Calluna vulgaris (pioneer 0-6 yr, building 6-14, mature 14-25, degenerate after 25; lives about 30-40 yr on dry heaths; seeds rarely germinate without light; highly shade-intolerant); Gimingham 1960 Biological Flora of the British Isles.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (flowers Jul-Sep, mauve, in racemes; capsule); FEIS (flowers Jul-Nov in N America, wind and animal dispersal, seed bank long-lived); Gimingham 1960 (bees and wind pollinate; capsules ripen in autumn and shed seed over winter); counts approximate.

growth.juvenile_note: A tiny seedling on wet sphagnum or sedge mats with small, leathery, rusty-scurfy oblong leaves. It becomes a low wiry sprig, then layers and spreads by rhizomes into a dense evergreen thicket (up to ~200 stems per m2) of arching stems carrying rows of small white urn-shaped bells in spring.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Chamaedaphne calyculata (evergreen to 1.5 m, dense clonal thickets, flowers Mar-Jul from buds formed the year before, one-sided racemes of 1-15+ flowers, persistent many-seeded capsules develop late summer-fall, seed set 50-95% with bees, germinates on sphagnum/sedge mats, shade intolerant); ages estimated

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Chamaedaphne calyculata (white urn flowers in one-sided racemes Mar-Jul, insect pollinated with bees, self-pollination only 1-15% seed set vs 50-95% open; round many-seeded capsules ripen late summer-fall and persist)

traits.leaf_shape: narrow grass blades in a dense tussock
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: culms with inflated bladeless sheaths; tussock of brown persistent sheaths

ground.silhouette: dense tussock with white cotton heads

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings need bare, wet, light-flooded peat (e.g. after fire): a hair-thin first leaf, then a tiny tuft of wiry leaves. New tillers form inside the old leaf sheaths, so the tuft slowly builds into a dense raised tussock of old sheaths and roots: about 3 years to first flowering, decades to full size. Each tiller lives ~7 years; the tussock goes on for a century or more.
growth.source: USDA FEIS species review (Eriophorum vaginatum): germination within ~20 days in light at 23-30 C; first flowering ~3 yr (Finland); tillers live 3-15 yr (mean 7-8); central Alaska tussocks average 158 yr old (Mark et al. 1985); shade intolerant. Tussock size-age curve estimated.

It adds tillers every year, building a dense round tussock of stiff stems that turns orange-brown in autumn and winter.

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds need winter cold, then germinate in spring on wet Sphagnum; the seedling is a tiny flat rosette of round red-haired leaves on long stalks. growth.source: USDA FEIS Drosera rotundifolia (short-lived perennial; flowers every summer once established, Jun-Sep, one flower opening per day; hibernaculum forms in fall and opens Apr-May; very shade intolerant; shallow roots <6 cm); Nordbakken et al. 2004 J.
